stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Complex multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature requiring full elaboration: real-time rendering, content binding, platform-specific behavior. openspec must run first to define AC and technical depth; speckit follows to harden with testability, security (XSS in preview rendering), and edge cases (connection drops, stale content, concurrent edits).

agentContributions.notes: Novel feature — the codebase has no live_preview config in the Contentstack Stack initialization. The LOCATED FIX SITE identifies src/services/contentstack.ts → options (line 69: contentstack.Stack(options)) as the attachment point. All downstream content fetching (getEntry, getSingleEntry, findSingletonEntry) flows through this Stack, so the change must plug in at the config level. useContent (236 callers) and every display component remain untouched; only the Stack init gains the live_preview property. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all nine criteria are new. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 cover the happy and off paths for env-var presence. (2) AC-3 is a critical safety gate — production must never serve draft content even if env vars leak. (3) AC-4 ensures the change is confined to Stack init and does not require downstream code changes in useContent or components. (4) AC-5 covers the empty-string edge case for the preview token, which is a common misconfiguration. (5) AC-6 makes the live preview protocol compliance observable by targeting outbound request shape. (6) AC-7 enforces cross-site parity since the story title specifies GO, UP, and MX. (7) AC-8 is a no-regression gate for the 236 useContent callers and display components. (8) AC-9 covers the invalid-host resilience case. CAVEAT: I have not read the file contents of src/services/contentstack.ts or the other listed files. The exact environment variable names, existing config structure, and Contentstack SDK version could affect precision — for example, whether `live_preview` is an object with `enable`/`preview_token`/`host` keys or a different shape. The criteria are written to be observable outcomes regardless of those details, but the implementer should validate the config shape against the actual SDK version in use.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Brownfield ticket — empty acceptanceCriteria is correct per policy; verificationCriteria are the observable surface and they are clear and testable (no-refresh update, within-seconds latency, all content types, concurrent entries). All four manifest paths verified as exact matches across all three codelines (gotransit, upexpress, metrolinx) with zero unresolved entries. Both agents added non-overlapping value: openspec identified the precise fix site (Stack init at line 69 in src/services/contentstack.ts) and correctly scoped the change to config-level only, noting the 236 useContent callers and display components remain untouched; speckit hardened the spec with production-safety gates (no draft content in prod), env-var edge cases (empty token), request-shape compliance, cross-site parity enforcement, no-regression coverage for existing callers, and invalid-host resilience. The file set is plausible for a live-preview config change: contentstack.ts for SDK config, useContent.ts for the fetching hook, contentCard.ts for type definitions, and ContentstackLink.tsx as a representative rendering component. speckit's caveat about not reading file contents is noted but does not constitute a spec defect. No concrete issues found.
